questions.text: आर्या और देव की पुस्तकें दर्शा रही हैं कि 31 मार्च, 2025 को उनकी विनियोजित पूँजी ₹9,00,000 थी । यदि सामान्य लाभ ₹ 45,000 हैं तथा अधिलाभ ₹ 27,000 हैं, तो प्रतिफल की सामान्य दर है :
questions.text_english: The books of Arya and Dev showed that their capital employed on 31st March, 2025 was ₹9,00,000. If the normal profits are ₹45,000 and super profits are ₹27,000, the normal rate of return is:
questions.solution: Option B is correct. The normal rate of return is calculated by expressing the normal profit as a percentage of the capital employed. Dividing the normal profit of ₹45,000 by the capital employed of ₹9,00,000 and multiplying the result by 100 yields a normal rate of return of exactly 5%.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। सामान्य प्रतिफल दर की गणना सामान्य लाभ को विनियोजित पूँजी के प्रतिशत के रूप में व्यक्त करके की जाती है। ₹45,000 के सामान्य लाभ को ₹9,00,000 की विनियोजित पूँजी से विभाजित कर 100 से गुणा करने पर 5% की सामान्य दर प्राप्त होती है।
questions.topic: Super Profit Method

questions.text: तुला, राम तथा माधवी एक फर्म के साझेदार थे। साझेदारी संलेख में साझेदारों के आहरण पर 12% प्रतिवर्ष ब्याज का प्रावधान था। फर्म प्रतिवर्ष अपने खाते 31 मार्च को बन्द करती है। 31 दिसम्बर, 2025 से शुरू करके माधवी ने प्रत्येक माह के अन्त में ₹ 40,000 का आहरण अपने व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए किया । माधवी के आहरण पर ब्याज होगा :
questions.text_english: Tula, Ram and Madhvi were partners in a firm. The partnership deed provided for interest on partners drawings @ 12% p.a. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. Starting from 31st December, 2025 Madhvi withdrew ₹40,000 at the end of every month for her personal use. Interest on Madhvi's drawings will be:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Madhvi made withdrawals at the end of each month from December to March, resulting in 4 equal withdrawals of ₹40,000, making the total drawings ₹1,60,000. Since the withdrawals are made at the end of the month, the average period is calculated as the sum of months left after the first drawing and the last drawing divided by two, which is 1.5 months. Applying the interest formula, ₹1,60,000 multiplied by 12% and then multiplied by 1.5/12 results in an interest amount of ₹2,400.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। माधवी ने दिसंबर से मार्च तक प्रत्येक महीने के अंत में ₹40,000 का आहरण किया, जिससे कुल आहरण ₹1,60,000 हो गया। चूँकि आहरण महीने के अंत में किए गए हैं, इसलिए औसत अवधि 1.5 महीने होगी। इस प्रकार, ₹1,60,000 का 12% की दर से 1.5 महीने का ब्याज ₹2,400 होता है।
questions.topic: Interest on Drawings

questions.text: ललिता, शिवानी तथा माधुरी एक फर्म की साझेदार थी तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटती थी । 31 मार्च, 2025 को माधुरी फर्म से सेवानिवृत्त हो गयी। सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि को उसके पूँजी खाते में ₹ 1,80,000 का शेष था। ललिता तथा शिवानी उसके दावे के पूर्ण निपटान में उसे ₹ 2,25,000 का भुगतान करने के लिए सहमत हो गईं। माधुरी की सेवानिवृत्ति पर फर्म की ख्याति थी :
questions.text_english: Lalita, Shivani and Madhuri were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. Madhuri retired from the firm on 31st March, 2025. The balance in her capital account on the date of her retirement was ₹1,80,000. Lalita and Shivani agreed to pay her ₹2,25,000 in full settlement of her claim. The goodwill of the firm on Madhuri's retirement was:
questions.solution: Option D is correct. The difference between the amount agreed to be paid to the retiring partner and the balance in her capital account represents her share of hidden goodwill. In this case, Madhuri's share of goodwill is the settlement amount of ₹2,25,000 less her capital balance of ₹1,80,000, which equals ₹45,000. Since Madhuri's profit-sharing ratio was 1/6, the total goodwill of the firm is calculated by multiplying her share of goodwill by the reciprocal of her profit share, resulting in ₹45,000 times 6, which equals ₹2,70,000.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। सेवानिवृत्त साझेदार को उसकी पूँजी शेष से अधिक दी जाने वाली राशि गुप्त ख्याति में उसके हिस्से को दर्शाती है। यहाँ माधुरी का ख्याति में हिस्सा ₹45,000 (₹2,25,000 - ₹1,80,000) है। चूँकि फर्म में उसका हिस्सा 1/6 था, अतः फर्म की कुल ख्याति ₹45,000 को 6 से गुणा करने पर ₹2,70,000 होगी।

questions.text: चमन तथा वाटिका एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4:5 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। उन्होंने फर्म के लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए मोहन को एक नये साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया। मोहन ने अपना भाग चमन तथा वाटिका से बराबर-बराबर अधिग्रहित किया। चमन, वाटिका तथा मोहन का नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: Chaman and Vatika were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:5. They admitted Mohan as a new partner for 1/5th share in the profits of the firm. Mohan acquired his share equally from Chaman and Vatika. The new profit sharing ratio of Chaman, Vatika and Mohan will be :
questions.solution: Option B is correct. Mohan is admitted for a 1/5th share, which he acquires equally from Chaman and Vatika, meaning he takes 1/10th from each. Chaman's new share is his old share of 4/9 minus the 1/10th he sacrificed, which equals 31/90. Vatika's new share is her old share of 5/9 minus the 1/10th she sacrificed, which equals 41/90. Mohan's share of 1/5 is equivalent to 18/90, making the new profit-sharing ratio 31:41:18.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। मोहन 1/5 हिस्से के लिए प्रवेश करता है, जिसे वह चमन और वाटिका से समान रूप से (1/10 प्रत्येक) प्राप्त करता है। चमन का नया हिस्सा 4/9 में से 1/10 घटाने पर 31/90 होगा। वाटिका का नया हिस्सा 5/9 में से 1/10 घटाने पर 41/90 होगा। मोहन का 1/5 हिस्सा 18/90 के बराबर है। अतः नया अनुपात 31:41:18 होगा।
questions.topic: New Profit Sharing Ratio

questions.text: सिद्धि, ज्ञान तथा गायत्री एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 31 मार्च, 2025 को उनकी फर्म का विघटन हो गया। विघटन के समय ₹25,000 के एक देनदार ने, जिसका ऋण पूर्व में डूबत ऋण के रूप में अपलिखित कर दिया गया था, राशि के 40% का भुगतान कर दिया । उपरोक्त लेनदेन के लिए लेखांकन होगा :
questions.text_english: Sidhi, Gyan and Gayatri were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:2. On 31st March, 2025 their firm was dissolved. At the time of dissolution a debtor amounting to ₹25,000 whose debt had been previously written off as bad debt paid 40% of the amount. The accounting treatment for the above transaction will be:

options.A: ₹10,000 डूबत ऋण वसूली खाते में क्रेडिट किये जायेंगे ।
options.B: ₹10,000 देनदार के व्यक्तिगत खाते में क्रेडिट किये जायेंगे ।
options.D: ₹10,000 डूबत ऋण खाते में क्रेडिट किए जायेंगे ।

options_english.A: ₹10,000 will be credited to bad debts recovered account.
options_english.B: ₹10,000 will be credited to the debtor's personal account.
options_english.C: ₹10,000 will be credited to realisation account.
options_english.D: ₹10,000 will be credited to bad debts account.

questions.solution: Option C is correct. In the event of the dissolution of a partnership firm, any amount recovered from a debtor whose debt was previously written off as a bad debt is considered a realization of an unrecorded asset. The recovered cash, which is 40% of ₹25,000 (amounting to ₹10,000), must be credited directly to the Realisation Account.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। फर्म के विघटन के समय, यदि कोई डूबत ऋण जो पहले अपलिखित कर दिया गया था, वसूल होता है, तो उसे एक गैर-लिखित परिसंपत्ति की वसूली माना जाता है। ₹25,000 का 40% (अर्थात ₹10,000) प्राप्त हुआ है, जिसे सीधे वसूली खाते (Realisation Account) में क्रेडिट किया जाएगा।
questions.topic: Realisation of Unrecorded Assets

questions.text:
सूर्या लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 50,000 समता अंशों का निर्गमन किया। राशि निम्न प्रकार से देय थी :
आवेदन पर ₹ 3 प्रति अंश
आबंटन पर ₹ 2 प्रति अंश
प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना पर - शेष
ऊषा ने, जिसे 700 अंश आबंटित किए गए थे, सम्पूर्ण अंश राशि का भुगतान आबंटन पर ही कर दिया । राज ने, जिसे 300 अंश आबंटित किए गए थे, प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना का भुगतान नहीं किया । प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना के लिए बैंक खाते में डेबिट की जाने वाली राशि उसके देय होने के बाद होगी :
questions.text_english:
Surya Ltd. issued 50,000 equity shares of ₹10 each. The amount was payable as follows:
on Application-₹3 per share
on Allotment-₹2 per share
on First and Final Call - the balance
Usha, to whom 700 shares were allotted, paid her entire share money on allotment. Raj, to whom 300 shares were allotted did not pay the first and final call. The amount to be debited to Bank Account for first and final call after it becomes due will be:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. The total due on the first and final call is ₹2,50,000, derived from 50,000 shares multiplied by the balance amount of ₹5 per share. Usha had already paid her call money of ₹3,500 in advance during the allotment phase, which will not be received again. Raj failed to pay his call money of ₹1,500. Subtracting the advance and the arrears from the total due amount leaves a net receipt of ₹2,45,000 to be debited to the Bank Account.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना पर कुल ₹2,50,000 देय हैं (50,000 अंश × ₹5)। ऊषा ने अपने 700 अंशों पर अग्रिम याचना (₹3,500) आबंटन के समय ही दे दी थी, इसलिए यह राशि दोबारा प्राप्त नहीं होगी। राज ने 300 अंशों पर याचना राशि (₹1,500) का भुगतान नहीं किया। अतः बैंक खाते में प्राप्त कुल राशि ₹2,50,000 - ₹3,500 - ₹1,500 = ₹2,45,000 होगी।
questions.topic: Calls in Arrears and Calls in Advance

questions.text: साक्षी लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 500 समता अंशों का, जिन्हें ₹ 2 प्रति अंश के प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित किया गया था, ₹ 4 प्रति अंश (प्रीमियम सहित) की दूसरी एवं अंतिम याचना का भुगतान न करने पर, हरण कर लिया। इन अंशों को अधिकतम कितनी छूट राशि पर पुनः निर्गमित किया जा सकता है ?
questions.text_english: Sakshi Ltd. forfeited 500 equity shares of ₹10 each, issued at a premium of ₹2 per share for non-payment of second and final call of ₹4 per share (including premium). The maximum amount of discount at which these shares can be reissued is:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. The maximum permissible discount on the reissue of forfeited shares is strictly equal to the amount originally received on those shares towards the share capital. Since the final call of ₹4 included the full ₹2 premium, the unpaid capital component was ₹2. Consequently, the paid-up capital component out of the ₹10 face value was ₹8. This ₹8 represents the maximum discount that can be offered per share upon reissue.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। हरण किए गए अंशों के पुनः निर्गमन पर अधिकतम छूट उतनी ही दी जा सकती है, जितनी राशि उन अंशों पर पूँजी के रूप में पहले ही प्राप्त हो चुकी है। अंतिम याचना के ₹4 में ₹2 प्रीमियम शामिल था, अर्थात पूँजी के ₹2 का भुगतान नहीं हुआ। इसलिए, ₹10 के अंकित मूल्य में से ₹8 प्रति अंश पूँजी के रूप में प्राप्त हो चुके थे, जो कि अधिकतम छूट की राशि है।
questions.topic: Reissue of Forfeited Shares

questions.text: निधि एवं कुनाल एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । उनकी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 3,00,000 तथा ₹ 2,00,000 थी। वे 6% वार्षिक दर से पूँजी पर ब्याज के अधिकारी थे। वर्ष के दौरान फर्म ने ₹ 15,000 का लाभ अर्जित किया । साझेदारों की पूँजी पर ब्याज होगा :
questions.text_english: Nidhi and Kunal were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:1. Their capitals were ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000 respectively. They were entitled to interest on capital @ 6% p.a. The firm earned a profit of ₹15,000 during the year. Interest on partners' capitals will be:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. The total interest on capital calculated at 6% would be ₹18,000 for Nidhi and ₹12,000 for Kunal, making a combined requirement of ₹30,000. However, the firm's available profit is only ₹15,000. When available profits are insufficient to cover full interest claims, the profit is distributed in the ratio of their respective interest claims, which is 18,000:12,000 or 3:2. Distributing the ₹15,000 profit in a 3:2 ratio yields ₹9,000 for Nidhi and ₹6,000 for Kunal.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। 6% की दर से निधि की पूँजी पर ब्याज ₹18,000 और कुनाल का ₹12,000 बनता है, जो कुल ₹30,000 है। लेकिन फर्म का कुल लाभ केवल ₹15,000 है, जो अपर्याप्त है। ऐसी स्थिति में, उपलब्ध लाभ को ब्याज के दावों के अनुपात (18,000 : 12,000 अर्थात् 3:2) में बाँटा जाता है। इस प्रकार, ₹15,000 को 3:2 में बाँटने पर निधि को ₹9,000 और कुनाल को ₹6,000 ब्याज मिलेगा।
questions.topic: Interest on Capital when Profit is Inadequate

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक विकल्प का उत्तर दें:
questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text: धरम, करम तथा रमन एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 7: 8:5 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 31 मार्च, 2025 को रमन फर्म से सेवानिवृत्त हो गया। धरम तथा करम ने भावी लाभों को 11:9 के अनुपात में बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। उनका अधिलाभ अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Dharam, Karam and Raman were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 7:8:5. On 31st March, 2025, Raman retired from the firm. Dharam and Karam decided to share profits in future in the ratio of 11:9. Their gaining ratio will be:
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The gaining ratio is calculated by subtracting the old profit-sharing ratio from the new profit-sharing ratio. For Dharam, the gain is 11/20 minus 7/20, which equals 4/20. For Karam, the gain is 9/20 minus 8/20, which equals 1/20. Comparing these fractions provides a gaining ratio of 4:1.

sub_questions.text: दीन, राजू तथा हरि एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 7: 6:7 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 31 मार्च, 2025 को राजू का देहान्त हो गया। दीन तथा हरि ने राजू के भाग को बराबर-बराबर लेने का निर्णय लिया। दीन तथा हरि के बीच नया लाभ-विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Deen, Raju and Hari were partners in a firm sharing profit and losses in the ratio of 7:6:7. On 31st March, 2025 Raju died. Deen and Hari decided to take over Raju's share equally. The new profit sharing ratio between Deen and Hari will be :
sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct. Raju's share was 6/20. Deen and Hari acquire this share equally, meaning each takes an additional 3/20. Adding this to their existing shares, Deen's new share becomes 7/20 plus 3/20, equaling 10/20. Hari's new share also becomes 7/20 plus 3/20, equaling 10/20. The resulting ratio is 10:10, which simplifies seamlessly to 1:1.

questions.text:
यहाँ दो कथन हैं, अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) :
अभिकथन (A) : साझेदारी समझौता साझेदारों के बीच संबंधों का आधार बन जाता है।
कारण (R) : साझेदारी दो या दो से अधिक व्यक्तियों के बीच व्यवसाय करने तथा इसके लाभ-हानि विभाजित करने के समझौते का परिणाम है।
निम्न में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
There are two statements Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Partnership Agreement becomes the basis of relationship among the partners.
Reason (R) : Partnership is the result of an agreement between two or more persons to do business and share its profits and losses.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

questions.text_english: Soni and Kush were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:5. Hitesh was admitted as a new partner for 1/5th share in the profits of the firm. After all adjustments regarding general reserve, goodwill, and gain on revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities, the balances in capital accounts of Soni and Kush were ₹7,00,000 and ₹13,00,000 respectively. Hitesh brought in proportionate capital for his 1/5th share in the profits of the firm. The amount of proportionate capital brought in by Hitesh was:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. The combined adjusted capital of the old partners, Soni and Kush, sums up to ₹20,00,000 (₹7,00,000 + ₹13,00,000). Since the new partner, Hitesh, is admitted for a 1/5th share in profits, the old partners retain the remaining 4/5ths of the firm's share. This indicates that 4/5ths of the total firm's capital is equivalent to ₹20,00,000. The total capital of the newly constituted firm would be ₹20,00,000 multiplied by 5/4, which equates to ₹25,00,000. Hitesh's proportionate capital requirement is 1/5th of this total, resulting in an amount of ₹5,00,000.

questions.text:
पिछले कुल वर्षों के दौरान एक फ़र्म के औसत लाभ ₹ 11,00,000 हैं। इसी प्रकार के व्यवसाय में प्रतिफल की सामान्य दर विनियोजित पूँजी की 10% है। व्यवसाय की परिसम्पत्तियाँ ₹ 90,00,000 तथा इनकी बाह्य देयताएँ ₹ 10,00,000 थीं।
फ़र्म की ख्याति की गणना कीजिए :
(i) अधिलाभों की पूँजीकरण विधि द्वारा
(ii) अधिलाभ विधि द्वारा यदि ख्याति का मूल्यांकन अधिलाभों के चार वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर किया जाए ।
questions.text_english:
Average profit of a firm during the last few years is ₹11,00,000. In similar business, the normal rate of return is 10% of the capital employed. Assets of the business were ₹90,00,000 and its external liabilities were ₹10,00,000. Calculate the value of goodwill by:
(i) Capitalisation of super profits method
(ii) Super profits method if the goodwill is valued at four years purchase of super profits.

key_points: Capital employed is calculated as Total Assets minus External Liabilities: ₹90,00,000 - ₹10,00,000 = ₹80,00,000.
Normal Profit is calculated as 10% of Capital Employed: 10% of ₹80,00,000 = ₹8,00,000.
Super Profit is Average Profit minus Normal Profit: ₹11,00,000 - ₹8,00,000 = ₹3,00,000.
(i) Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits = Super Profit × (100 / NRR) = ₹3,00,000 × (100 / 10) = ₹30,00,000.
(ii) Goodwill by Super Profit Method = Super Profit × Number of years' purchase = ₹3,00,000 × 4 = ₹12,00,000.

questions.solution: First, we determine the capital employed by subtracting the external liabilities of ₹10,00,000 from the total assets of ₹90,00,000, resulting in ₹80,00,000. The normal profit is then calculated as 10% of this capital employed, yielding ₹8,00,000. Subtracting this normal profit from the firm's average profit of ₹11,00,000 gives a super profit of ₹3,00,000. Under the capitalisation of super profits method, goodwill is evaluated by capitalizing the super profit at the normal rate of return (₹3,00,000 divided by 10%), resulting in ₹30,00,000. Alternatively, utilizing the super profit method based on four years' purchase, goodwill is the super profit multiplied by 4, which equates to ₹12,00,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सबसे पहले विनियोजित पूँजी की गणना की जाती है, जो कि कुल संपत्तियों (₹90,00,000) में से बाह्य देयताओं (₹10,00,000) को घटाने पर ₹80,00,000 प्राप्त होती है। सामान्य लाभ विनियोजित पूँजी का 10% अर्थात् ₹8,00,000 है। औसत लाभ ₹11,00,000 में से इस सामान्य लाभ को घटाने पर अधिलाभ ₹3,00,000 प्राप्त होता है। (i) अधिलाभों की पूँजीकरण विधि के अनुसार ख्याति = अधिलाभ × (100/10) = ₹30,00,000 होगी। (ii) अधिलाभ विधि के अंतर्गत 4 वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर ख्याति = ₹3,00,000 × 4 = ₹12,00,000 होगी।

sub_questions.text: रौनक कॉटन लिमिटेड ने हैवी मशीन्स लिमिटेड से ₹ 6,80,000 की मशीनरी क्रय की। हैवी मशीन्स लिमिटेड को ₹50 प्रत्येक के 10,500 समता अंशों को 20% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करके तथा शेष का एक चैक द्वारा भुगतान किया गया। रौनक कॉटन लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपरोक्त लेनदेनों के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Raunak Cotton Ltd. purchased machinery of ₹6,80,000 from Heavy Machines Ltd. The Payment to Heavy Machines Ltd. was made by issuing 10,500 equity shares of ₹50 each at a premium of 20% and the balance through a cheque. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Raunak Cotton Ltd.

key_points: Machinery A/c Dr. ₹6,80,000 To Heavy Machines Ltd. ₹6,80,000 (Purchase of machinery)
Calculation of share issue value: 10,500 shares × ₹60 (₹50 face value + ₹10 premium) = ₹6,30,000.
Balance payment by cheque: Total ₹6,80,000 - Share value ₹6,30,000 = ₹50,000.
Heavy Machines Ltd. Dr. ₹6,80,000 To Equity Share Capital A/c ₹5,25,000 (10,500 × ₹50), To Securities Premium A/c ₹1,05,000 (10,500 × ₹10), To Bank A/c ₹50,000 (Payment made)

sub_questions.solution: The transaction begins with the acquisition of the asset, documented by debiting the Machinery Account and crediting Heavy Machines Ltd. for the purchase consideration of ₹6,80,000. For the settlement, the company issues 10,500 equity shares with a face value of ₹50 at a 20% premium, making the issue price ₹60 per share. This share issuance accounts for ₹6,30,000 of the liability (Equity Share Capital is credited with ₹5,25,000 and Securities Premium is credited with ₹1,05,000). The outstanding balance of ₹50,000 (₹6,80,000 minus ₹6,30,000) is paid via cheque. Thus, the second journal entry debits Heavy Machines Ltd. for the full ₹6,80,000, while crediting Equity Share Capital, Securities Premium, and the Bank Account for their respective amounts.

sub_questions.text: नीयो लिमिटेड ने मदुरा लिमिटेड से ₹25,00,000 की परिसम्पत्तियों तथा ₹ 12,00,000 की देयताओं का अधिग्रहण ₹ 18,00,000 के क्रय प्रतिफल के बदले किया। नीयो लिमिटेड ने क्रय प्रतिफल के सम्पूर्ण भुगतान में ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 11% ऋणपत्रों को 10% बट्टे पर निर्गमित किया । नीयो लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपरोक्त लेनदेनों के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Neo Ltd. took over assets of ₹25,00,000 and liabilities of ₹12,00,000 of Madura Ltd. for a purchase consideration of ₹18,00,000. Neo Ltd. issued 11% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 10% in full satisfaction of the purchase consideration. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Neo Ltd.

key_points: Calculation of Goodwill/Capital Reserve: Net Assets taken over = ₹25,00,000 - ₹12,00,000 = ₹13,00,000. Since the Purchase Consideration (₹18,00,000) is greater than the net assets, the difference of ₹5,00,000 is treated as Goodwill.
Entry 1: Sundry Assets A/c Dr. ₹25,00,000, Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹5,00,000 To Sundry Liabilities ₹12,00,000, To Madura Ltd. ₹18,00,000.
Calculation of number of debentures: Purchase Consideration of ₹18,00,000 divided by issue price of ₹90 per debenture = 20,000 debentures.
Entry 2: Madura Ltd. Dr. ₹18,00,000, Discount on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr. ₹2,00,000 To 11% Debentures A/c ₹20,00,000.

sub_questions.solution: The business acquisition is recorded by first determining the value of net assets taken over, which is ₹13,00,000 (Assets of ₹25,00,000 less Liabilities of ₹12,00,000). Since Neo Ltd. agreed to a purchase consideration of ₹18,00,000, the excess ₹5,00,000 represents the Goodwill acquired. The initial journal entry debits Sundry Assets with ₹25,00,000 and Goodwill with ₹5,00,000, while crediting Sundry Liabilities for ₹12,00,000 and Madura Ltd. for ₹18,00,000. To settle the purchase consideration, the company issues debentures at a 10% discount, making the issue price ₹90 per debenture. Dividing the ₹18,00,000 obligation by ₹90 indicates 20,000 debentures are required. The settlement entry debits Madura Ltd. for ₹18,00,000 and Discount on Issue of Debentures for ₹2,00,000, crediting 11% Debentures Account with the total face value of ₹20,00,000.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text: सुल्तान, सिंह तथा तुलसी एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 9:7:4 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । उनकी स्थायी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 6,00,000; ₹ 5,00,000 तथा ₹ 4,00,000 थी । साझेदारी संलेख में पूँजी पर 10% वार्षिक ब्याज देने का प्रावधान था। वर्ष के अंतिम खाते तैयार करने के पश्चात् यह पाया गया कि पूँजी पर 12% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज लगाया गया है। आवश्यक समायोजन रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Sultan, Singh and Tulsi were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 9:7:4. Their fixed capitals were ₹6,00,000, ₹5,00,000 and ₹4,00,000. The partnership deed provided that interest on partners capital accounts will be allowed at 10% per annum. After the final accounts for the year were prepared, it was found that interest on capital was allowed @ 12% per annum. Pass the necessary adjusting journal entry.

key_points: Identify the error: Interest was credited at 12% instead of 10%, resulting in an excess credit of 2%.
Calculate the 2% excess interest on fixed capitals: Sultan = ₹12,000, Singh = ₹10,000, Tulsi = ₹8,000. Total excess = ₹30,000.
Reverse the excess by debiting the partners for these amounts and distributing the total ₹30,000 back as profit in their 9:7:4 ratio.
Profit distribution: Sultan gets ₹13,500, Singh gets ₹10,500, Tulsi gets ₹6,000.
Net effect: Sultan is credited ₹1,500, Singh is credited ₹500, and Tulsi is debited ₹2,000.
Entry: Tulsi's Current A/c Dr. ₹2,000 To Sultan's Current A/c ₹1,500, To Singh's Current A/c ₹500. (Current accounts are used as capitals are fixed).

sub_questions.solution: The error occurred because the partners were credited with 12% interest on their fixed capitals instead of the correct 10%. This means an excess of 2% was wrongfully distributed as interest. For Sultan, the excess is ₹12,000; for Singh, it is ₹10,000; and for Tulsi, it is ₹8,000, aggregating to a total of ₹30,000. Correcting this involves taking back the excess interest, which creates a firm profit of ₹30,000 that must be redistributed in their profit-sharing ratio of 9:7:4. Accordingly, Sultan is entitled to a profit share of ₹13,500, Singh to ₹10,500, and Tulsi to ₹6,000. Comparing the amounts to be taken back with the amounts to be credited reveals a net position where Tulsi must be debited by ₹2,000, while Sultan and Singh must be credited by ₹1,500 and ₹500, respectively. The final adjusting journal entry is passed through their Current Accounts since their capital accounts are maintained under the fixed method.

sub_questions.text: समीर तथा मनवीर एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को उन्होंने लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए संदीप को ₹ 80,000 की न्यूनतम गारंटी राशि के साथ एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया। समीर तथा मनवीर ने पहले की तरह ही लाभों को बाँटना जारी रखा परन्तु संदीप को दी गयी गारंटी के कारण हुई किसी भी कमी को 3:5 के अनुपात में वहन करने पर सहमति हुई। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का शुद्ध लाभ ₹ 3,20,000 था । 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए समीर, मनवीर तथा संदीप का लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाता तैयार कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Sameer and Manveer were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3. On 1st April, 2024, they admitted Sandeep as a new partner for 1/5th share in the profits with a guaranteed minimum amount of ₹80,000. Sameer and Manveer continue to share profits as before but agreed to bear any deficiency on account of guarantee to Sandeep in the ratio of 3:5. The net profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2025 was ₹3,20,000. Prepare Profit and Loss Appropriation Account of Sameer, Manveer and Sandeep for the year ended 31st March, 2025.

key_points: Sandeep's normal share of profit = 1/5 of ₹3,20,000 = ₹64,000.
Deficiency in Sandeep's share = Guaranteed amount ₹80,000 - ₹64,000 = ₹16,000.
This deficiency is borne by Sameer and Manveer in a 3:5 ratio. Sameer bears 3/8 of ₹16,000 = ₹6,000. Manveer bears 5/8 of ₹16,000 = ₹10,000.
Remaining profit for old partners = ₹3,20,000 - ₹64,000 = ₹2,56,000. Shared in their old 5:3 ratio. Sameer gets 5/8 = ₹1,60,000. Manveer gets 3/8 = ₹96,000.

sub_questions.solution: First, Sandeep's base share of the ₹3,20,000 net profit is calculated as 1/5th, giving him ₹64,000. Since he has a minimum guarantee of ₹80,000, there is a deficiency of ₹16,000. This deficiency is agreed to be borne by Sameer and Manveer in the ratio of 3:5, obligating Sameer to sacrifice ₹6,000 and Manveer to sacrifice ₹10,000. Out of the total profit, the remaining ₹2,56,000 is initially allocated to Sameer and Manveer in their old ratio of 5:3, yielding ₹1,60,000 for Sameer and ₹96,000 for Manveer. In the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account, the net profit of ₹3,20,000 is credited. On the debit side, Sameer's capital is credited with his net share of ₹1,54,000 (after deducting his ₹6,000 sacrifice), Manveer's capital is credited with ₹86,000 (after deducting his ₹10,000 sacrifice), and Sandeep's capital receives his fully guaranteed ₹80,000.

questions.text:
आदित्य तथा आनंद एक फ़र्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । साझेदारी संलेख में प्रावधान था कि आनंद को शुद्ध लाभ पर 10% कमीशन देय होगा। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष का फर्म का शुद्ध लाभ ₹ 2,00,000 था ।
आनंद को कमीशन देने तथा इसे लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाते में हस्तांतरित करने के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ दीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Aditya and Anand were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:1. The partnership deed provided that Anand is to be allowed a commission of 10% on net profit. The net profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2025 was ₹2,00,000.
Pass necessary journal entries for allowing commission to Anand and transfer of the same to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.

key_points: Anand's commission calculation: 10% of the net profit of ₹2,00,000, which equals ₹20,000.
Entry to allow commission: Commission A/c Dr. ₹20,000 To Anand's Capital A/c ₹20,000 (Allowing commission).
Entry to transfer commission: Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c Dr. ₹20,000 To Commission A/c ₹20,000 (Transferring commission expense).

questions.solution: The partner's commission must be computed as 10% of the net profit before any such charges. Given a net profit of ₹2,00,000, Anand's commission amounts to ₹20,000. The first journal entry formally allows the commission by debiting the Partner's Commission Account and crediting Anand's Capital Account with ₹20,000. Following this, the expense must be closed at year-end. The second journal entry transfers this commission by debiting the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account and crediting the Partner's Commission Account with ₹20,000.

1 अप्रैल, 2024 को दिव्या लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 10,000, 8% ऋणपत्रों को 6% बट्टे पर निर्गमित करने के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किये। इन ऋणपत्रों का शोधन 5 वर्षों के पश्चात् 10% प्रीमियम पर करना था । निर्गमन पूर्णरूप से अभिदत्त हुआ तथा सभी आवेदकों को पूर्णरूप से ऋणपत्रों का आबंटन कर दिया गया। 31 मार्च, 2025 को कम्पनी की पुस्तकों में प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते में ₹9,000 का शेष था।
8% ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन तथा ऋणपत्र निर्गमन पर हुई हानि को अपलिखित करने के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए। 'ऋणपत्र निर्गमन हानि खाता' भी तैयार कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
On 1st April, 2024 Divya Ltd. invited applications for issuing 10,000, 8% debentures of ₹10 each at a discount of 6%. These debentures were redeemable at a premium of 10% after five years. The issue was fully subscribed and the debentures were allotted in full to all the applicants. On 31st March, 2025 the company had a balance of ₹9,000 in its Securities Premium Account.
Pass necessary journal entries for the issue of 8% Debentures and writing off Loss on issue of Debentures. Also prepare 'Loss on Issue of Debentures Account'.

key_points: Face value of debentures = 10,000 × ₹10 = ₹1,00,000.
Discount on issue (6%) = ₹6,000. Premium on redemption (10%) = ₹10,000. Total Loss on Issue = ₹16,000.
Entry 1: Bank A/c Dr. ₹94,000 To Debenture Application & Allotment A/c ₹94,000.
Entry 2: Debenture Application & Allotment A/c Dr. ₹94,000, Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr. ₹16,000 To 8% Debentures A/c ₹1,00,000, To Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c ₹10,000.
Writing off loss: Total loss ₹16,000 is met primarily by Securities Premium (₹9,000) and the rest from Statement of P&L (₹7,000).
Entry 3: Securities Premium A/c Dr. ₹9,000, Statement of Profit & Loss Dr. ₹7,000 To Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c ₹16,000.
Loss on Issue of Debentures Account will show a debit entry of ₹16,000 against the issue, subsequently credited by SPR and P&L at year-end.

questions.solution: The face value of the 10,000 debentures is ₹1,00,000. A 6% discount means ₹6,000 is deducted upon issue, and a 10% premium on redemption means an additional ₹10,000 liability must be recognized. This yields a total Loss on Issue of Debentures amounting to ₹16,000. The receipt is recorded by debiting the Bank Account and crediting Debenture Application & Allotment Account with the net proceeds of ₹94,000. Next, to record the allotment and corresponding liabilities, the Debenture Application & Allotment Account is debited for ₹94,000 and the Loss on Issue of Debentures Account is debited for ₹16,000, while the 8% Debentures Account is credited for its face value of ₹1,00,000 and the Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account is credited for ₹10,000. To write off the total loss of ₹16,000, the available Securities Premium balance of ₹9,000 is exhausted first, and the remaining ₹7,000 is charged to the Statement of Profit & Loss. Thus, Securities Premium and Statement of P&L are debited, and Loss on Issue of Debentures is credited. The required ledger account for Loss on Issue will display the debited ₹16,000 linked to the issuance and the matching credits closing it out at year-end.

questions.text:
किरन, रवीना तथा हिना एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । फर्म प्रतिवर्ष अपनी पुस्तकें 31 मार्च को बन्द करती है। साझेदारी संलेख की शर्तों के अनुसार, किसी भी साझेदार की मृत्यु पर फर्म की ख्याति की गणना पिछले तीन वर्षों के औसत लाभ के चार गुना के आधार पर की जाएगी। 1 जुलाई, 2025 को हिना की मृत्यु हो गयी। पिछले तीन वर्षों के लाभ थे :
2022-23 ₹4,75,000
2023-24 ₹4,05,000
2024-25 ₹3,20,000
मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में हिना के भाग की गणना पिछले वर्ष के लाभ के आधार पर की जाएगी।
(i) फर्म की ख्याति की तथा ख्याति में हिना के भाग की गणना कीजिए ।
(ii) मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभों में हिना के भाग की गणना कीजिए ।
(iii) ख्याति खाता खोले बिना ख्याति के लेखांकन तथा हिना की मृत्यु के समय लाभ में उसके भाग के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Kiran, Raveena and Hina were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. As per the terms of the partnership deed, on the death of any partner, the goodwill of the firm will be calculated on the basis of four times the average profits of the last three years. Hina died on 1st July 2025. The Profits for the last three years were:
2022-23 ₹4,75,000
2023-24 ₹4,05,000
2024-25 ₹3,20,000
Hina's share of profit upto the date of death was to be calculated on the basis of previous year's profit.
(i) Calculate goodwill of the firm and Hina's share of goodwill.
(ii) Calculate Hina's share in the profits of the firm till the date of her death.
(iii) Pass necessary journal entries for the treatment of goodwill without opening goodwill account and for Hina's share of profit at the time of her death.

key_points: (ii) Hina survived for 3 months in the current year (April, May, June). Hina's profit share = Previous year's profit × Time proportion × Her share = ₹3,20,000 × 3/12 × 2/10 = ₹16,000.
(iii) Goodwill adjustment entry: Debit continuing partners in gaining ratio (5:3). Kiran's Capital A/c Dr. ₹2,00,000; Raveena's Capital A/c Dr. ₹1,20,000 To Hina's Capital A/c ₹3,20,000.
(iii) Profit share entry: Profit and Loss Suspense A/c Dr. ₹16,000 To Hina's Capital A/c ₹16,000.

questions.solution: First, the firm's average profit over the preceding three years must be calculated. The sum of the profits (₹4,75,000, ₹4,05,000, and ₹3,20,000) equates to ₹12,00,000, yielding an average profit of ₹4,00,000. The firm's total goodwill, determined as four times this average, amounts to ₹16,00,000. Hina's individual share of this goodwill, based on her 2/10 ratio, is ₹3,20,000. Secondly, since Hina died on 1st July, she survived for 3 months of the new financial year. Her share of the profit till death, based on the previous year's profit of ₹3,20,000, is calculated as ₹3,20,000 multiplied by 3/12 and then by 2/10, resulting in ₹16,000. Lastly, the journal entries must reflect these adjustments. The goodwill is adjusted by debiting Kiran's and Raveena's Capital Accounts in their gaining ratio of 5:3 for ₹2,00,000 and ₹1,20,000 respectively, while crediting Hina's Capital Account for ₹3,20,000. Her interim profit is accounted for by debiting the Profit and Loss Suspense Account and crediting her Capital Account with ₹16,000.

[Table of Balance Sheet: Liabilities: Creditors ₹7,00,000; Capitals: Seema ₹9,00,000, Raveena ₹11,00,000. Total Liabilities = ₹27,00,000. Assets: Cash at Bank ₹2,00,000, Stock ₹4,00,000, Debtors ₹6,00,000, Plant & Machinery ₹15,00,000. Total Assets = ₹27,00,000.]
उपरोक्त तिथि को फर्म का विघटन हो गया। संयन्त्र तथा मशीनरी को पुस्तक मूल्य से 20% कम पर तथा स्टॉक को ₹ 3,90,000 में बेचा गया। देनदारों से पूरी राशि वसूल हो गयी। रवीना सभी वसूली व्ययों को वहन करने के लिए सहमत हो गई जिसके लिए उसे ₹ 10,000 का कमीशन दिया गया । वास्तविक वसूली व्यय ₹ 8,000 थे ।
वसूली खाता तथा साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते तैयार कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Seema and Raveena were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 11: 9. On 31st March, 2025, their Balance Sheet was as follows: 
On the above date the firm was dissolved. Plant and Machinery was sold at 20% less than the book value and stock at ₹3,90,000. Debtors were realised in full. Raveena agreed to bear all realisation expenses for which she was allowed a commission of ₹10,000. Actual realisation expenses amounted to ₹8,000.
Prepare Realisation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Transfer of assets to Realisation A/c debit side (excluding cash): Stock 4L, Debtors 6L, P&M 15L = Total 25L.
Transfer of Creditors to Realisation A/c credit side: 7L.
Realisation values: P&M (15L less 20%) = 12L, Stock = 3.9L, Debtors (full) = 6L. Total cash realised = 21.9L credited to Realisation A/c.
Payment of liabilities: Creditors paid in full = 7L debited to Realisation A/c.
Raveena's Commission: ₹10,000 debited to Realisation A/c and credited to Raveena's Capital A/c. Actual expenses of ₹8,000 are personal and ignored.
Realisation Loss calculation: Debit total (25L + 7L + 0.10L = 32.1L) minus Credit total (7L + 21.9L = 28.9L) = Loss of ₹3,20,000.
Distribution of Loss in 11:9 ratio: Seema = ₹1,76,000; Raveena = ₹1,44,000.
Partners' Capital Accounts closing balances: Seema = 9L - 1.76L = ₹7,24,000 to be paid. Raveena = 11L + 0.10L (comm) - 1.44L = ₹9,66,000 to be paid.

questions.solution: In the Realisation Account, begin by transferring all tangible assets except cash to the debit side at their book values, totaling ₹25,00,000. Transfer the Creditors to the credit side at ₹7,00,000. Next, record the realization of assets on the credit side via the Bank Account: Plant and Machinery at a 20% discount fetches ₹12,00,000, Stock brings ₹3,90,000, and Debtors realize fully at ₹6,00,000, creating total cash proceeds of ₹21,90,000. On the debit side, record the full payment of Creditors via the Bank Account for ₹7,00,000. Additionally, debit the Realisation Account with Raveena's commission of ₹10,000. The actual realization expenses of ₹8,000 are borne by Raveena personally and require no entry in the firm's books. Balancing the Realisation Account reveals a total debit of ₹32,10,000 and a credit of ₹28,90,000, resulting in a realization loss of ₹3,20,000. This loss is distributed in their 11:9 ratio, debiting Seema's Capital Account with ₹1,76,000 and Raveena's Capital Account with ₹1,44,000. Finally, in the Partners' Capital Accounts, opening balances are brought down, Raveena is credited with her commission, and the realization losses are debited. The accounts are closed by making final bank payments of ₹7,24,000 to Seema and ₹9,66,000 to Raveena.

sub_questions.text_english:
Generic Pharma Ltd. invited applications for using 3,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹6 per share. The amount was payable as follows:
on Application and Allotment - ₹4 per share (including premium of ₹2 per share)
on First and Final Call - Balance
Applications for 4,00,000 shares were received. Applications for 40,000 shares were rejected and the application money was refunded. Shares were allotted on pro-rata basis to the remaining applicants. Excess money received on applications was adjusted towards sums due on first and final call. Jain, an applicant for 3,600 shares failed to pay the first and final call. His shares were forfeited.
Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Generic Pharma Ltd. for the above transactions. Open 'calls in arrears account' and 'calls in advance account', wherever necessary.

key_points: Total application money received = 4,00,000 shares × ₹4 = ₹16,00,000.

Allotment of 3,00,000 shares utilizes ₹12,00,000 (Capital ₹6,00,000 + Premium ₹6,00,000). 40,000 shares rejected mean a refund of ₹1,60,000. Excess advance transferred to Calls in Advance = ₹2,40,000.
First and Final Call due = 3,00,000 shares × ₹12 (Capital ₹8 + Premium ₹4) = ₹36,00,000.
Jain applied for 3,600 shares. His allotted shares = (3,00,000 / 3,60,000) × 3,600 = 3,000 shares.
Jain's arrears: Due on call = 3,000 × ₹12 = ₹36,000. Less advance (600 excess shares × ₹4 = ₹2,400). Net arrears = ₹33,600.
Bank receipt on call = ₹36,00,000 - ₹2,40,000 (total advance) - ₹33,600 (arrears) = ₹33,26,400.
Forfeiture Entry: Share Capital Dr. ₹30,000 (3,000 × 10), SPR Dr. ₹12,000 (unpaid premium 3,000 × 4) To Calls in Arrears ₹33,600, To Share Forfeiture ₹8,400.

sub_questions.solution: First, the total application money for 4,00,000 shares at ₹4 per share is received, amounting to ₹16,00,000. When allotting the 3,00,000 available shares, ₹6,00,000 is transferred to Share Capital and ₹6,00,000 to Securities Premium. The ₹1,60,000 associated with the 40,000 rejected shares is immediately refunded through the Bank. The residual balance of ₹2,40,000 from the pro-rata applicants is transferred into the Calls in Advance account. The First and Final Call is then made due for ₹36,00,000 (3,00,000 shares multiplied by the balance of ₹12, which comprises ₹8 capital and ₹4 premium). To determine Jain's arrears, his allotted shares are calculated by finding the pro-rata ratio: out of 3,60,000 applicants, 3,00,000 were allotted, so his 3,600 applied shares result in 3,000 allotted shares. His 600 excess applied shares translate to an advance of ₹2,400. His call due was ₹36,000, leaving net arrears of ₹33,600 to be debited to Calls in Arrears. The bank subsequently receives the net call amount of ₹33,26,400. Finally, upon forfeiture of Jain's 3,000 shares, Share Capital is debited with ₹30,000 and Securities Premium with the unpaid ₹12,000, while Calls in Arrears is credited with ₹33,600 and Share Forfeiture is credited with his actual paid amount of ₹8,400.

Out of these, 600 shares were reissued as fully paid up in such a way that ₹4,200 was transferred to capital reserve. (ii) Ashoka Ltd. forfeited 2,000 equity shares of ₹100 each issued at a premium of 10% for non-payment of allotment money of ₹60 per share (including premium). The first and final call of ₹20 per share was not yet made. The forfeited shares were re-issued at ₹70 per share fully paid up.

key_points: (i) Forfeiture: Share Capital Dr. ₹30,000 To Calls in Arrears ₹6,000, To Share Forfeiture ₹24,000.

(i) Calculation of Reissue Price: Share forfeiture corresponding to 600 shares is ₹4,800. If ₹4,200 is transferred to Capital Reserve, the discount utilized is ₹600. Reissue entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹5,400, Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. ₹600 To Share Capital ₹6,000.
(ii) Forfeiture: Called-up capital is ₹80 per share. Share Capital Dr. ₹1,60,000, Securities Premium Dr. ₹20,000 To Share Allotment ₹1,20,000, To Share Forfeiture ₹60,000.

Since the entire ₹60,000 in the Share Forfeiture account was used up as discount upon reissue, the transfer to Capital Reserve is strictly Nil.

sub_questions.solution: In the case of Diksha Ltd., the forfeiture is recorded by debiting Share Capital for the full face value of ₹30,000, and crediting Calls in Arrears for ₹6,000 alongside Share Forfeiture for ₹24,000. When 600 of these shares are reissued, their proportional forfeited amount stands at ₹4,800. Given that ₹4,200 is transferred to Capital Reserve, exactly ₹600 must have been utilized as a reissue discount. Consequently, the reissue entry debits the Bank Account for ₹5,400 and Share Forfeiture for ₹600, crediting Share Capital with ₹6,000. For Ashoka Ltd., the called-up capital rests at ₹80 per share. The forfeiture entry debits Share Capital with ₹1,60,000 and Securities Premium with ₹20,000, while crediting Share Allotment with ₹1,20,000 and Share Forfeiture with the paid-up balance of ₹60,000. Upon the reissue of all 2,000 shares at ₹70 fully paid, a discount of ₹30 per share is given. The corresponding entry debits the Bank Account for ₹1,40,000 and Share Forfeiture for ₹60,000, crediting Share Capital for ₹2,00,000. Since the forfeiture account is entirely depleted by the discount, no subsequent transfer to Capital Reserve occurs.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text: संजय तथा विजय एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4:3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2025 को उन्होंने फर्म के लाभों में 2/5 भाग के लिए बाबुल को एक नए साझेदार के रूप में फर्म में प्रवेश दिया। बाबुल के प्रवेश पर निम्नलिखित पर सहमति हुई : (i) संजय, विजय तथा बाबुल का नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात 3:3:4 होगा। (ii) फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन पिछले तीन वर्षों के औसत लाभ के चार वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर किया जायेगा । पिछले तीन वर्षों के लाभ थे : 2022-23 ₹16,500, 2023-24 ₹17,500, 2024-25 ₹18,500। (iii) बाबुल ख्याति प्रीमियम का अपना भाग नगद लायेगा जिसके आधे का संजय तथा विजय द्वारा आहरण किया जायेगा । (iv) बाबुल के प्रवेश पर परिसम्पत्तियों के पुनर्मूल्यांकन तथा देयताओं के पुनर्निर्धारण के परिणामस्वरूप ₹ 70,000 की हानि हुई । (v) बाबुल के प्रवेश पर फर्म में ₹ 28,000 का सामान्य संचय था । (vi) ख्याति, पुनर्मूल्यांकन पर हुई हानि तथा सामान्य संचय से सम्बन्धित सभी आवश्यक समायोजनों के पश्चात् संजय तथा विजय के पूँजी खाते क्रमशः ₹ 3,50,000 तथा ₹ 2,50,000 का शेष दर्शा रहे थे। बाबुल फर्म के लाभों में अपने 2/5 भाग के लिए आनुपातिक पूँजी लाया । अपने कार्य (गणनाओं) को स्पष्ट रूप से दर्शाते हुए बाबुल के प्रवेश पर उपरोक्त लेनदेनों के लिए फर्म की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Sanjay and Vijay were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3. On 1st April, 2025 they admitted Babul as a new partner for 2/5th share in the profits of the firm. On Babul's admission, the following was agreed upon : (i) The new profit sharing ratio of Sanjay, Vijay and Babul will be 3:3:4. (ii) The goodwill of the firm will be valued at four years purchase of the average profits of the last three years. The profits of the previous three years were : 2022-23 ₹16,500, 2023-24 ₹17,500, 2024-25 ₹18,500. (iii) Babul will bring his share of goodwill premium in cash, half of which will be withdrawn by Sanjay and Vijay. (iv) On Babul's admission, revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities resulted in a loss of ₹70,000. (v) At the time of Babul's admission, the firm had a General Reserve of ₹28,000. (vi) After making necessary adjustments relating to goodwill, loss on revaluation and general reserve, the capital accounts of Sanjay and Vijay showed balances of ₹3,50,000 and ₹2,50,000 respectively. Babul brought proportionate capital for his 2/5th share in the profits of the firm. Showing your workings clearly pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the firm on Babul's admission.

key_points: Sacrificing ratio: Sanjay = 4/7 - 3/10 = 19/70. Vijay = 3/7 - 3/10 = 9/70. The ratio is definitively 19:9.
Goodwill evaluation: Average profit = ₹17,500. Firm Goodwill = 17,500 × 4 = ₹70,000. Babul's share is ₹28,000.
General Reserve and Revaluation Loss are distributed to Sanjay and Vijay in their old 4:3 ratio.
Goodwill Premium entry: Babul brings ₹28,000. It is credited to Sanjay (₹19,000) and Vijay (₹9,000). Half of this is withdrawn: Sanjay Dr. ₹9,500, Vijay Dr. ₹4,500 To Bank ₹14,000.

Capital calculation: Total adjusted capital of old partners = ₹3,50,000 + ₹2,50,000 = ₹6,00,000. This represents a 3/5th share. Total firm capital = ₹10,00,000. Babul's capital is therefore ₹4,00,000.
Final Bank Entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹4,28,000 To Babul's Capital A/c ₹4,00,000, To Premium for Goodwill A/c ₹28,000.

sub_questions.solution: First, we establish the sacrificing ratio between Sanjay and Vijay by subtracting their new shares from their old shares, which results in a clear 19:9 ratio. Next, we value the firm's goodwill by taking the average of the three years' profits (₹17,500) and multiplying it by four years' purchase, yielding a total firm goodwill of ₹70,000. Babul's 2/5th share of this goodwill premium amounts to ₹28,000. To clear the balance sheet, the existing General Reserve of ₹28,000 and the Revaluation Loss of ₹70,000 are formally distributed to Sanjay and Vijay in their old profit-sharing ratio of 4:3. When Babul introduces his goodwill premium in cash, it is credited to the old partners according to their 19:9 sacrificing ratio, granting Sanjay ₹19,000 and Vijay ₹9,000. A subsequent entry records their withdrawal of half of this amount, debiting their accounts and crediting cash for ₹14,000. To ascertain Babul's required capital contribution, we combine the fully adjusted capital balances of the old partners (₹3,50,000 and ₹2,50,000) to get ₹6,00,000. Since this sum corresponds to their combined 3/5ths share of the newly structured firm, the total firm capital evaluates to ₹10,00,000. Babul must bring in 2/5ths of this total, which strictly equals ₹4,00,000. The ultimate journal entry debits the Bank Account to record the inflow of both his capital and the premium for goodwill.

sub_questions.text: अनुज, दिविज़ तथा शिल्पा एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 2: 1: 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । 31 मार्च, 2023 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्न प्रकार था : [Table of Balance Sheet: Capitals Anuj ₹3,00,000, Divij ₹4,00,000, Shilpa ₹5,00,000. Bills Payable ₹60,000. Creditors ₹1,20,000. Assets: Land & Building ₹8,00,000, Furniture ₹2,40,000, Stock ₹1,20,000, Debtors ₹1,70,000, Cash ₹50,000.] उपरोक्त तिथि को निम्नलिखित शर्तों पर अनुज फर्म से सेवानिवृत्त हो गया : (i) ख्याति में अनुज के भाग का मूल्य ₹ 90,000 था और इसका लेखांकन ख्याति खाता खोले बिना किया जाना था। (ii) परिसम्पत्तियों के पुनर्मूल्यांकन तथा देयताओं के पुनर्निर्धारण के परिणामस्वरूप ₹25,000 का लाभ हुआ । (iii) अनुज़ को देय राशि उसके ऋण खाते में स्थानान्तरित की जानी थी जिसका भुगतान 31 मार्च, 2024 से प्रारम्भ करके दो बराबर वार्षिक किस्तों में 12% वार्षिक ब्याज दर सहित किया जाएगा। साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते तथा अनुज का ऋण खाता तैयार कीजिए जब तक उसका पूर्णरूप से भुगतान न कर दिया जाए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Anuj, Divij and Shilpa were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:1:2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2023 was as follows: Anuj retired on the above date on the following terms: (i) Anuj's share of goodwill was valued at ₹90,000 and the same was to be treated without opening goodwill account. (ii) Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities resulted in a gain of ₹25,000. (iii) Amount due to Anuj was transferred to his loan account, to be paid in two equal yearly instalments plus interest @ 12% p.a. on the unpaid balance starting from 31st March, 2024. Prepare Partners' Capital Accounts and Anuj's Loan Account till it is fully discharged.

key_points: Capital Account updating: Distribute revaluation gain of ₹25,000 in 2:1:2 (Anuj ₹10,000, Divij ₹5,000, Shilpa ₹10,000).
Goodwill accounting: Anuj's ₹90,000 share is borne by Divij and Shilpa in their gaining ratio of 1:2. Divij is debited ₹30,000 and Shilpa is debited ₹60,000.
Anuj's final settlement balance: Base capital ₹3,00,000 + Reval gain ₹10,000 + Goodwill ₹90,000 = ₹4,00,000 transferred to his Loan Account.
Anuj's Loan Account Year 1: Starting principal ₹4,00,000. Add 12% interest (₹48,000). Payment made is ₹2,00,000 principal plus ₹48,000 interest = ₹2,48,000. Closing balance is ₹2,00,000.
Anuj's Loan Account Year 2: Starting principal ₹2,00,000. Add 12% interest (₹24,000). Final payment made is ₹2,24,000, bringing the loan balance to nil.

sub_questions.solution: In the Capital Accounts, we start with the opening balances of ₹3,00,000, ₹4,00,000, and ₹5,00,000. The revaluation gain of ₹25,000 is distributed in their 2:1:2 ratio, adding ₹10,000 to Anuj, ₹5,000 to Divij, and ₹10,000 to Shilpa. For the goodwill adjustment, Anuj receives his ₹90,000 share, which is debited from Divij and Shilpa in their gaining ratio of 1:2, meaning Divij is debited ₹30,000 and Shilpa is debited ₹60,000. Anuj's fully adjusted capital balance totals exactly ₹4,00,000, which is immediately transferred to his Loan Account. Moving to Anuj's Loan Account, the opening balance is recorded as ₹4,00,000. At the end of the first year, a 12% interest charge of ₹48,000 is accrued. The first installment payment consists of half the principal (₹2,00,000) plus the interest, totaling ₹2,48,000, leaving a carry-forward balance of ₹2,00,000. At the close of the second year, 12% interest on the remaining principal amounts to ₹24,000. The final payment of ₹2,24,000 is recorded, which completely discharges the loan and balances the account to zero.

Statement - II: In case of financial enterprises receipts of interest and dividend are classified as investing activities.

options.B: कथन I सत्य है तथा कथन II असत्य है।
options.C: कथन I असत्य है तथा कथन II सत्य है।

sub_questions.text_english:
Classify the following items under major heads and sub-heads (if any) in the Balance Sheet of the company as per Schedule III Part I of the Companies Act 2013:
(i) Vehicles
(ii) Provision for taxation
(iii) Work in progress

key_points: (i) Vehicles: Major Head - Non-Current Assets; Sub-head - Property, plant and equipment.
(ii) Provision for taxation: Major Head - Current Liabilities; Sub-head - Short-term provisions.
(iii) Work in progress: Major Head - Current Assets; Sub-head - Inventories.

sub_questions.solution: In accordance with Schedule III Part I of the Companies Act 2013, the items are classified meticulously as follows: (i) Vehicles represent tangible operational assets, so they are classified under the major head 'Non-Current Assets' with the sub-head 'Property, plant and equipment'. (ii) Provision for taxation refers to impending tax liabilities payable within a year, making its major head 'Current Liabilities' with the sub-head 'Short-term provisions'. (iii) Work in progress represents partially finished goods meant for sale, placing it under the major head 'Current Assets' with the sub-head 'Inventories'.

sub_questions.text: 'रडॉर चार्ट्स' क्या हैं? ये किस उद्देश्य की पूर्ति करते हैं ?

key_points: Radar charts are graphical methods of displaying multivariate data in the form of a two-dimensional chart of three or more quantitative variables.

सूचना: कुल परिसम्पत्तियाँ ₹6,00,000, अचल देयताएँ ₹1,40,000, अंशधारक निधियाँ ₹4,20,000, अचल परिसम्पत्तियाँ ₹5,20,000
sub_questions.text_english:
From the following information, calculate: (i) Current ratio and (ii) Debt to capital employed ratio
Information: Total Assets ₹6,00,000, Non-Current Liabilities ₹1,40,000, Shareholders' Funds ₹4,20,000, Non-current Assets ₹5,20,000

key_points: Current Assets = Total Assets - Non-Current Assets = ₹6,00,000 - ₹5,20,000 = ₹80,000.
Total Liabilities match Total Assets = ₹6,00,000. Current Liabilities = Total Assets - (Shareholders' Funds + Non-Current Liabilities) = ₹6,00,000 - (₹4,20,000 + ₹1,40,000) = ₹40,000.
(i) Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = ₹80,000 / ₹40,000 = 2:1.
Capital Employed = Shareholders' Funds + Non-Current Liabilities = ₹4,20,000 + ₹1,40,000 = ₹5,60,000.
(ii) Debt to Capital Employed Ratio = Long-term Debt (Non-Current Liabilities) / Capital Employed = ₹1,40,000 / ₹5,60,000 = 0.25:1.

sub_questions.solution: First, we deduce Current Assets by subtracting the given Non-Current Assets from the Total Assets, which evaluates to ₹6,00,000 minus ₹5,20,000, resulting in ₹80,000. Applying the fundamental balance sheet equation, Total Liabilities and Equity equal Total Assets. Therefore, Current Liabilities are found by subtracting Shareholders' Funds (₹4,20,000) and Non-Current Liabilities (₹1,40,000) from the Total Assets (₹6,00,000), yielding exactly ₹40,000. The Current Ratio calculates to ₹80,000 divided by ₹40,000, which is 2:1. Next, Capital Employed is aggregated by adding Shareholders' Funds and Non-Current Liabilities, totaling ₹5,60,000. The Debt to Capital Employed Ratio evaluates Non-Current Liabilities against this Capital Employed, mathematically represented as 1,40,000 divided by 5,60,000, yielding a precise ratio of 0.25:1.

sub_questions.text:
निम्नलिखित सूचना से गणना कीजिए: (i) ऋण-समता अनुपात; तथा (ii) कुल परिसम्पत्तियों पर ऋण अनुपात

sub_questions.text_english:
From the following information, calculate: (i) Debt-Equity Ratio and (ii) Total Assets to Debt ratio
Information: Long-term borrowings ₹8,00,000, Other long-term liabilities ₹80,000, Long term provisions ₹1,20,000, Share capital ₹24,00,000, Reserves and Surplus ₹6,00,000, Non-current Assets ₹36,00,000, Current Assets ₹14,00,000, Current Liabilities ₹10,00,000

key_points: Total Long-term Debt = Long-term borrowings + Other long-term liabilities + Long term provisions = ₹8,00,000 + ₹80,000 + ₹1,20,000 = ₹10,00,000.
Equity (Shareholders' Funds) = Share capital + Reserves and Surplus = ₹24,00,000 + ₹6,00,000 = ₹30,00,000.
(i) Debt-Equity Ratio = Debt / Equity = ₹10,00,000 / ₹30,00,000 = 0.33:1.
Total Assets = Non-current Assets + Current Assets = ₹36,00,000 + ₹14,00,000 = ₹50,00,000.
(ii) Total Assets to Debt ratio = Total Assets / Debt = ₹50,00,000 / ₹10,00,000 = 5:1.

sub_questions.solution: The total long-term debt is systematically calculated by summing long-term borrowings, other long-term liabilities, and long-term provisions (₹8,00,000 + ₹80,000 + ₹1,20,000), which precisely equals ₹10,00,000. Total Equity represents the aggregation of Share Capital and Reserves & Surplus, accumulating to ₹30,00,000. The Debt-Equity Ratio is therefore derived by dividing ₹10,00,000 by ₹30,00,000, equating to a simplified ratio of 0.33:1. To establish Total Assets, one must combine Non-current Assets and Current Assets (₹36,00,000 + ₹14,00,000), supplying a sum of ₹50,00,000. The Total Assets to Debt ratio is subsequently formulated by dividing the overarching ₹50,00,000 by the total long-term debt of ₹10,00,000, returning a clear 5:1 metric.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain any two ways in which Computerized Accounting System safeguards the secrecy of business data.

key_points: Password Protection: Assigning unique user IDs and passwords to restrict access only to authorized personnel.
Data Encryption: Scrambling data into an unreadable format that can only be deciphered with a specific decryption key, protecting it from external hackers.

sub_questions.solution: A Computerized Accounting System reliably safeguards proprietary data utilizing two prominent strategies: Password Protection and Data Encryption. Password protection systematically ensures that solely authorized personnel possessing specific, secure login credentials can access the accounting software, thereby mitigating the risk of internal unauthorized viewing. Concurrently, data encryption scrambles the natively stored or transmitted financial data into an intricate, unreadable code format. This ensures that even if external malicious actors intercept the network data, they fundamentally cannot decipher the information without possessing the exact decryption key.

sub_questions.solution: The interactive table engineered to quickly summarize extensive amounts of data is formally known as a Pivot Table. प्रचालन गतिविधियों से रोकड़ प्रवाह की गणना कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
For the year ended 31st March 2025, Sona Ltd. made a profit of ₹4,00,000 after charging depreciation of ₹75,000 on fixed assets and a transfer of ₹1,50,000 to general reserve. Goodwill written off during the year was ₹80,000. The company sold machinery of the book value of ₹90,000 at ₹95,000. During the year, trade receivables increased by ₹40,000 and trade payables increased by ₹30,000. Prepaid expenses increased by ₹2,000 and outstanding wages decreased by ₹20,000.
Calculate cash flows from operating activities.

key_points: Net Profit after appropriations is given as ₹4,00,000.
Add: Transfer to General Reserve ₹1,50,000. Resulting Net Profit before Tax and Extraordinary Items = ₹5,50,000.
Adjustments for Non-Cash/Non-Operating expenses: Add Depreciation ₹75,000. Add Goodwill written off ₹80,000.
Less: Gain on sale of machinery (₹95,000 selling price - ₹90,000 book value) = ₹5,000.
Operating Profit before Working Capital Changes = ₹5,50,000 + ₹1,55,000 - ₹5,000 = ₹7,00,000.
Working Capital Adjustments: Less Increase in Trade Receivables ₹40,000. Add Increase in Trade Payables ₹30,000. Less Increase in Prepaid Expenses ₹2,000. Less Decrease in Outstanding Wages ₹20,000.
Cash Flow from Operating Activities definitively evaluates to: ₹7,00,000 - ₹40,000 + ₹30,000 - ₹2,000 - ₹20,000 = ₹6,68,000.

sub_questions.solution: Commence the statement derivation with the provided post-appropriation profit of ₹4,00,000. To accurately deduce the Net Profit before Tax, proactively add back the ₹1,50,000 transferred to the General Reserve, culminating in ₹5,50,000. Subsequently, adjust for non-cash and non-operating accounting items: progressively add back the Depreciation expense of ₹75,000 and the amortized Goodwill written off of ₹80,000. Concurrently, carefully deduct the Non-Operating Gain derived from the sale of machinery amounting to ₹5,000 (calculated via the ₹95,000 selling price against the ₹90,000 book value). This framework yields a precise Operating Profit before Working Capital Changes equalling ₹7,00,000. The final phase involves methodical working capital modifications: directly subtract the operative increase in Trade Receivables (₹40,000), add the corresponding increase in Trade Payables (₹30,000), subtract the incremental rise in Prepaid Expenses (₹2,000), and firmly subtract the tangible decrease in Outstanding Wages (₹20,000). The finalized Cash Flow exclusively driven by Operating Activities mathematically calculates to exactly ₹6,68,000.

sub_questions.text_english: What is data formatting? What tools are used to format a data? Explain.

key_points: Data formatting refers to changing the visual appearance and layout of data to make it more readable, understandable, and presentable without changing the underlying actual values.
Font Tools: Options to change typeface, size, bold, italics, underline, and color to emphasize specific data points.
Alignment Tools: Control horizontal (left, center, right) and vertical alignment, wrap text, and merge cells to structure layout.
Number Formatting Tools: Define how numbers display, such as adding currency symbols, percentage signs, comma separators, or controlling decimal places.
Border and Fill Tools: Apply distinct border lines to cells and background fill colors to delineate headers and specific datasets.
Conditional Formatting: Automatically format cells based on specific logical criteria or rules to highlight trends or anomalies visually.

sub_questions.solution: Data formatting constitutes the comprehensive process of meticulously altering the visual appearance and organizational layout of raw data. It fundamentally aims to render information highly readable, easily understandable, and professionally presentable, entirely without permanently changing the spreadsheet's underlying mathematical values. To achieve this, several distinct software tools are utilized. Font Tools provide direct options to modify typeface, textual size, bolding, italics, underlining, and text color, strategically emphasizing specific key data points. Alignment Tools govern the rigid horizontal (left, center, right) and vertical positioning of text, incorporating text wrapping and cell merging to synthesize a coherent structural layout. Number Formatting Tools rigorously dictate how mathematical values visually display, seamlessly allowing users to insert currency symbols, percentage signs, decimal constraints, and comma separators. Border and Fill Tools apply crisp boundary lines and thematic background colors to delineate headers securely from core datasets. Finally, Conditional Formatting stands out as an advanced tool that autonomously adjusts a cell's format based entirely on predefined logical criteria, acting swiftly to visually spotlight significant trends or data anomalies.
